sentences.text: The appellants - original claimants have preferred this appeal under section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act C/FA/2394/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act")
being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the judgment and award dated 21.4.2009 passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Ahmedabad in Motor Accident Claims Petition No.1043 of 2003.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Petition No.1043 of 2003
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case that emerge from the record of the appeal are as under.

2.1 That on 19.9.2003 deceased Rameshchandra Joshi was travelling as a pillion rider on a scooter bearing registration No.GJ 1 AV 2441 which was driven by the opponent No.1 and they were travelling from Madhur Hotel Cross Roads to Vikram Park

. That when they reached near Krishnagar, Parshvanath Township, the offending vehicle i.e. one mini door rickshaw came from Naroda side rashly and negligently and dashed with the hand cart of the vegetable vendor and then dashed at the back side of the scooterist which caused serious head injuries to deceased Rameshchandra Joshi.
That the deceased was shifted to Shardaben Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries.
C/FA/2394/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023
The offence was registered at Naroda Police Station, Ahmedabad.

3. The claimants i.e. wife, children and mother of deceased Rameshchandra Joshi preferred the claim petition mainly contending that the impugned judgement and award passed by the learned Tribunal is improper and unjust to some extent and against the provisions of the law and facts and circumstances of the case.
That the deceased was working in Reliance Industries and was earning Rs.4290/- per month.

That the claimants have spent a huge amount for funeral and last rites of the deceased but due to his sad demise, they have lost their source of income and hence, the claimants have claimed compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- jointly and severally from the opponents.
4.

The opponent - insurance company appeared before the learned Tribunal and after the evidence was recorded, the learned Tribunal was pleased to award an amount of Rs.3,38,000/- to the claimants as compensation by a judgment and award dated 21.4.2009.
C/FA/2394/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 5.

Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the said judgment and award, the claimants have preferred the present appeal mainly contending that the amount awarded has resulted in miscarriage of justice as the learned Tribunal has failed to appreciate the future prospects of advancement in life and career of the deceased while computing the total amount of just and appropriate compensation.

That the learned Tribunal has considered the amount of income of the deceased at Rs.3000/- per month but has not considered his future prospective income which ought to have been considered at Rs.5525/- per month and hence, the quantum of compensation awarded is on lower side.

That the learned Tribunal ought to have awarded the entire amount of Rs.6,00,000/- to the claimants and hence, the appellants have prayed that the amount of compensation be enhanced with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till the deposit of enhanced amount before the learned Raskshaben Rameshchandra Joshi vs Nilesh Subhashbhai Sheth on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2428915/
2 Tribunal.
6.

sentences.text:
I have heard Mr.Hiren Modi, learned advocate for C/FA/2394/2009 JUDGMENT DATED:
16/06/2023 the appellants and Mr.Dakshesh Mehta, learned advocate for the respondent No.4.
7. Mr.

Hiren Modi, learned advocate for the appellants has submitted that the learned Tribunal has not considered the future prospective income of the deceased which ought to have been at 30% of Rs.4290/- and after applying multiplier of 14 and deducting 1/4th amount for personal expenses,
the dependency loss would come to Rs.7,02,702/-.

Moreover, the learned Tribunal has also not considered the loss of estate which is at Rs.15000/- and funeral expenses have not been granted,
whereas the claimants are entitled to funeral expenses at Rs.15,000/-.

The learned Tribunal has also grossly erred in granting Rs.20,000/- towards loss of consortium when in fact, there are three dependents, the amount of Rs.40000 x 3 = Rs.1,20,000/- ought to have been granted to the claimants and instead of the amount of Rs.3,38,000/-, an amount of Rs.8,52,702/- ought to have been granted to the claimants in view of the settled law of the Honourable Supreme Court C/FA/2394/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.
8.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Mr.Dakshesh Mehta, learned advocate for respondent No.4 - insurance company has opposed the present appeal and has submitted that learned Tribunal has considered all the aspects and if ultimately this Court comes to the conclusion that the amount of compensation is to be enhanced in favour of the claimants, interest at the rate of 6% per annum may be granted on the same.
9.

The Honourable Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (supra) has observed thus :
"59.3 While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

59.4 In case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where C/FA/2394/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10%
where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

10. The learned Tribunal considered the notional income of the deceased at Rs.36,000/- p.a. but the claimants have examined Narendrabhai Chandulal Patel at Exh.42 to prove the income of the deceased and the salary slip of the deceased for the month of May 2003 is produced wherein the salary of the deceased is shown to be Rs.4290/- p.m.

The learned Tribunal has also not considered Raskshaben Rameshchandra Joshi vs Nilesh Subhashbhai Sheth on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2428915/
3 the future prospective income of the cased.

sentences.text: In view of the above cited judgment, the future prospective income of the deceased and 30% rise in income of Rs.4290/- per month is required to be added as the deceased was self employed and after deducting 1/4th for personal expenses of the deceased and applying the multiplier of 14 as per the judgment of the Honourable Apex Court in the case of Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the total dependency loss C/FA/2394/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 would come to Rs.7,02,702/-, the learned Tribunal has also not granted any amount towards the loss of estate and funeral expenses, but in fact, the claimants are entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the learned Tribunal has also awarded the amount of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of consortium to the claimant No.1 and Rs.10,000/- each to claimant Nos.2 and 3, but as per the settled law in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), the wife is entitled to Rs.40,000/- as spousal consortium and minor children are also entitled to Rs.40,000/- each as parental consortium and accordingly, the claimants are entitled to Rs.1,20,000/- towards loss of consortium.
11. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the compensation awarded by learned Tribunal is held to be not just and adequate and thereby the same deserves to be modified as under.

Sr.No Details Rs.
1

Dependency loss 7,02,702/-
 C/FA/2394/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 2

Funeral expenses 15,000/-
3 Loss of estate 15,000/-
4 Consortium 1,20,000/-
The learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.3,38,000/- and hence, the claimants shall be entitled for an additional amount of Rs.5,14,702/-.

The learned Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum on the amount awarded as compensation and the learned advocates appearing for the respective insurance companies have strongly opposed the grant of interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum on the enhanced amount.

The accident had occurred on 19.9.2003 and the award came to be passed by the learned Tribunal on 21.4.2009 and in view of the above, this Court is of the considered opinion that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced amount is granted, it would meet the ends of justice.
13. Resultantly, the appeal is partly allowed.

The claimants shall be entitled to an additional amount of Rs.5,14,702/- with 6% interest from the date of application C/FA/2394/2009 JUDGMENT Raskshaben Rameshchandra Joshi vs Nilesh Subhashbhai Sheth on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2428915/
4 DATED: 16/06/2023 till the realization.

sentences.text: The respondent No.4 insurance company is hereby directed to deposit the additional sum of Rs.5,14,702/- with 6% interest within a period of 12 weeks after receipt of the copy of the order.
Rest of the judgment and award remains unaltered.
The claimants have to deposit the court fees on the enhanced amount.
The learned Tribunal, in turn, shall disburse the same in favour of the claimants after proper verification.
R & P be sent back forthwith.
